spec: DESIGN.md — the answer guarantee and its evidence levels; docs/how-to-use.md — what arrangement-unverified tells a client. The per-core marks in docs/research/coverage-matrix.md are a different record: which cores were checked where, not whether the arrangement itself was ever observed. The 'label' here is a sentence fragment for caveat prose ('no live installation of an EmuDeck arrangement has been observed'), NOT the project's display name — that is the 'label' in distribution_labels.json, which a client renders on its own; the two coincide for retrodeck and for nothing else.
description: Which emulator arrangements atlas has observed on a live installation, keyed by installation kind. An arrangement's config reading is source-verified against pinned upstream either way — this file records only whether a real machine running that arrangement has confirmed the wiring end to end. An arrangement with no entry counts as unverified: nothing here is evidence by omission.

retrodeck.label: RetroDECK

verified.reference: the RetroDECK 0.10.9b installation atlas's live verification round ran against (docs/research/retrodeck-save-placement.md; per-core records in core_audit.json)

retrodeck.note: [V] Save roots, the override chain, the ES-DE catalogue and the firmware tree were read off a running installation and compared against the resolver's answers.

emudeck.label: an EmuDeck arrangement

verified.reference: the EmuDeck installation atlas's live verification round ran against. The version is the backend checkout's git HEAD, read as the two plain files under ~/.config/EmuDeck/backend/.git (the HEAD symref, then the loose ref) — the same read the runtime drift comparison performs. The deployed ES-DE was 3.4.1, established out-of-band: the AppImage's md5 matched the stable LinuxSteamDeckAppImage package in ES-DE's published latest_release.json (the check is scripts/verify_esde_evidence.py — run it on the reference machine to re-establish or refute this identification; re-run CONFIRMED it on 2026-08-19); ~/ES-DE/logs/es_log.txt states the version in its first line only after a first launch, and the verification machine had none

emudeck.note: [V] Detection, the marker parse, the ES-DE catalogue (the 8-system overlay, gamelist selections, the sealed state), ROM placement, the RetroArch save/state wiring ($savesPath/retroarch/{saves,states} symlinked into the Flatpak tree, cfg naming the symlink) and the firmware root were read off a running installation and compared against the resolver's answers. ES-DE presence is decided from the disk; a machine driven by Pegasus or Steam ROM Manager instead keeps the emulator-catalogue-unestablished refusal.

bare_retroarch_flatpak.label: the bare RetroArch Flatpak
bare_retroarch_flatpak.note: [D] The cfg location and RetroArch's own upstream defaults are source-verified; no unclaimed org.libretro.RetroArch installation has been observed.

bare_retroarch_native.label: a native RetroArch install
bare_retroarch_native.note: [D] The cfg location and RetroArch's own upstream defaults are source-verified; no native installation has been observed.
